summary: 0.2.1 release closure advanced through every non-blocked authorized step. Both public 0.2.1 packages were re-verified without republishing; the existing v0.2.1 annotated tag and public GitHub Release resolve to the accepted product commit 2ea15a0f7a676dbf073b0b5bdbd90c15b1df4281; the real web Harness is left with dsh-plugin-image-mind@0.2.1 active and @ran-sh/dsh-vision@0.2.1 present through official lifecycle tooling; composition, host boot, settings route, catalog route, and rendered plugin-client smoke passed. A configured provider was exercised opaquely through the real UI: image upload, user message, and understand_image tool-stage markers passed, but no normal assistant reply arrived within the bounded 180-second wait, so that optional hosted-provider check is PARTIAL. The sole mandatory blocker is npm authentication: registry ping passed but npm whoami returned E401, so neither exact 0.2.0 deprecation could be attempted safely. Both 0.2.0 versions remain published and not deprecated. ACTIVE_TASK.json is retained, PR #65 remains Draft/unmerged, and no secret material was accessed or exposed.

These public tarball identities exactly match the already-accepted Batch 023 candidate evidence, including its prior byte-for-byte lib/** comparison. No npm publish command was run.

tests.evidence: The public packaged command npx -y dsh-plugin-image-mind@0.2.1 status --profile web reported exact DSH 0.1.1-rc.2, plugin installed 0.2.1 with active layer, and service @ran-sh/dsh-vision present 0.2.1. Final status remained identical, leaving 0.2.1 installed and active.

tests.name: real-harness-host-route-and-rendered-ui-smoke
tests.evidence: A task-owned DSH web process booted the real web profile on a dedicated localhost port and reported readiness. Headless browser navigation reached the rendered UI; GET /image-mind/config and GET /image-mind/catalog both returned HTTP 200; the DOM contained exactly one image-mind plugin client style marker, proving the packaged browser module executed. Only boolean/HTTP evidence was retained. The task-owned process was stopped and its port verified closed; the installed plugin was not removed.

tests.name: optional-real-ui-hosted-provider-visual-smoke
tests.evidence: The redacted settings surface was inspected only as booleans and confirmed an active provider with complete=true and keyReady=true; no provider id, endpoint, model, key, or secret was printed. In a new UI session, an in-memory 16x16 solid-color PNG was pasted and sent with a non-sensitive color prompt. Browser evidence showed the /image-mind/attach upload request, a new user message, and the understand_image tool-stage marker. No normal assistant row arrived within the bounded 180-second wait, so the required understand_image -> vision -> normal assistant completion was not proven and is recorded PARTIAL, not PASS. This optional check is not the mandatory release blocker.

tests.name: final-public-and-github-state
tests.evidence: Final read-only registry state remained unchanged: both 0.2.1 versions are public/latest; both 0.2.0 versions remain published and not deprecated; no unexpected versions or tags appeared. v0.2.1 and its GitHub Release still identify the accepted product commit. Draft PR #65 remained open, unmerged, on chore/0201-publish-deprecate-023; all checks on its pre-result head c83f124f28b0394dc4e4ebf287be8295942ea814 were SUCCESS.

blockers: The two mandatory npm deprecations cannot be performed from the current unauthenticated npm session: npm whoami returns E401. An interactive maintainer authentication ceremony or an already-authenticated publish-capable session is required. After authentication, only the exact two authorized 0.2.0 deprecations and their immediate read-only verification remain mandatory before the task can become PASS.
notes: ACTIVE_TASK.json is intentionally retained because mandatory deprecation acceptance is incomplete; delete_active_task_on_completion therefore does not apply to this blocked result.

No npm republish/unpublish, dist-tag/access/visibility mutation, force-push, history rewrite, product edit, new PR, self-merge, manual Harness profile edit, or plugin removal occurred.

No secret material was requested, inspected, printed, logged, copied, or committed. Public package metadata, public GitHub identifiers, version numbers, boolean readiness, and HTTP status evidence only are recorded.

The webapp-testing procedure was followed with a safe fallback from unavailable Python Playwright to the bundled Node Playwright driving installed Edge in headless mode; no browser package was downloaded or installed.
